tonight.headline: Lost, 103.8 to 119.7. Third straight loss, and it came from injuries, not the lineup
body: Every one of your starters is finished and Footballers are already 15.9 ahead with Stafford still to play, so the week is decided; ESPN shows 1%. You'll be 0-3.

There's nothing to set tonight. The real news since the last brief is bad: Miami's coach said Achane's knee 'does not sound very optimistic', and Jefferson was ruled out in the third quarter. The two cards below are next week's answer.

case.label: What changed since 16:30
case.body: Achane: Miami coach Hafley said 'it does not sound very optimistic at this moment', MRI Monday (PFT, 27 Sep, postgame). Jefferson: downgraded to out in the third quarter after a defender fell on his right ankle; he finished with 2 catches for 32 (Vikings.com; AP via Yahoo). Coker says he doesn't think the quad is bad (NBC). The Vikings D/ST finished on 17 and Pineiro on 8.

case.label: Was the lineup wrong?
case.body: No. The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. McLaurin (19.7) and Tuten (17.0) outscored injured starters from the bench, but only hindsight picks those swaps.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing on the scoreboard: Stafford can only add to their total. What changes next week is Monday's MRI.

doFirst.title: If Achane misses Week 4: start Tuten in his RB slot
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed until Miami rule on the MRI, but Miami's coach already sounds pessimistic. A swap; nobody is dropped.

case.label: The knee
case.body: Non-contact, left knee, third carry of the game (CBS). After the game Miami coach Hafley said 'it does not sound very optimistic at this moment' and called it a serious injury. The MRI is Monday (PFT, 27 Sep). ESPN has not priced any of this into Week 4 yet.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: He's Jacksonville's lead back: 15 carries, 73 yards and a TD on 48% of snaps in a 35-6 win (Florio), with Lawrence throwing three touchdowns (AP). Monangai missed Wednesday and Thursday with a knee before a full Friday (Eagles.com report) and splits Chicago's work with Swift; Kamara shares New Orleans' backfield with Etienne. Next week's projection makes the final call between them.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Rosters unlock after Monday night. The MRI result should land Monday; Miami's first practice report is Wednesday.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The MRI is clean and Achane is cleared for Week 4, so the card never fires. If it fires, it's graded on the outcome: the back who starts in Achane's slot against the best bench alternative that week.

case.body: 9 targets in each of the last two weeks, and 6 for 77 and a TD in Mariota's first start (NBC). One watch point: Hogs Haven report Daniels could be back within three weeks, so the passer may change again.

whatWentWrong.title: Three starters hurt mid-game
whatWentWrong.lead: Achane (knee), Coker (quad) and Jefferson (ankle). All were started correctly, and together they scored 10.7 on 51.5 projected.

case.label: Not a lineup miss
case.body: The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. Coker's pregame ankle wasn't what took him out: it was a new quad injury. Achane's was a non-contact knee on his third carry, and Jefferson's a defender landing on his ankle.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Week 4 depends on three medical reports, and Achane's already sounds bad (Hafley, postgame). The two cards above settle the replacements now, so Monday and Wednesday are a checklist.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: All three are cleared for Week 4. Then both cards stay unarmed.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · The Big Lead · AtoZ Sports

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker-over-McLaurin flex call lost, 3.8 to 19.7
whatWentWrong.lead: Closed WRONG. The falsifier fired: Coker got 4 targets while Mariota threw McLaurin 9.

case.label: The call
case.body: On 21 Sep the brief moved Coker into the flex because Daniels' injury meant Mariota would start. The falsifier said the call was wrong if Coker drew under five targets while McLaurin drew eight or more. Coker got 4 before the quad took him out (The Big Lead). McLaurin got 9 (NBC).

case.label: The honest part
case.body: The injury cut Coker's day short, and that doesn't rescue the call. A lineup decision is graded on its outcome, and this one lost by 15.9. The theory that Mariota would starve McLaurin was wrong on its first test.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The flex slot reopens. Week 4's projection decides it, and the second card makes McLaurin the first replacement if a receiver is out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Week 3 archive disagreeing with the reported target counts. The archive grades it formally on Tuesday.

worthALook.name: Ollie Gordon II
worthALook.ownership: not in the snapshot's wire list
worthALook.lead: Miami's back if Achane's MRI is as bad as the coach sounds. Tuesday's decision, not tonight's.

case.label: The role
case.body: With Jaylen Wright inactive (foot), Gordon took over after Achane went down: 17 carries for 41 and a touchdown, plus 3 catches (CBS, 27 Sep). Hafley's postgame words on Achane were 'not very optimistic'.

case.label: Why not a card
case.body: He's not rostered anywhere in Chem, but the snapshot's ~110-player wire list doesn't include him, so I can't see whether he's a free agent or on waivers, or when he'd clear. The waiver tool didn't print him either: it reads Weeks 1-2, and his role began today. Never invent a deadline.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday's run, if Monday's MRI puts Achane out for weeks and Wright's foot is still a question. Chem priority resets weekly, so a claim costs nothing lasting. The drop would be Kamara, the lowest-projected back.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A clean MRI, or Jaylen Wright back at full practice Wednesday, which makes Gordon the RB2 in a committee.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN projected Pineiro 9.4 and McPherson 7.4 this week. Pineiro finished on 8 in a 36-30 win over Arizona; Cincinnati lost 30-27 at Pittsburgh.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep. The seat's seven-day churn window runs until 30 Sep.

case.label: When to act
case.body: After 30 Sep, and only if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson finishes top five.

worthALook.name: Lions D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison. Hold the Vikings.

case.body: Both projected 7.7. The Vikings finished on 17, holding Tampa to 16 (AP).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Third D/ST in a week already, and the incumbent just scored 17. There's no gap to act on.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only on a Week 4 projection gap of two points or more, after the churn window closes.

case.label: What would change it

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest players you could move, and nobody on the wire clears either. That's two weeks of data, which is thin. Achane's knee could change the RB question by Tuesday, so that run should re-check it.
